proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(a\in I\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\), \(p_x>0\), so all conditional expectations below are well defined for this cell.  Let \((\mathcal V,\mathscr V)\), \(V\), and \(h\) be supplied by \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), and let
\[
 K_x(C)=P(V\in C\mid X=x),
 \qquad
 g_x(u)=\int_{\mathcal V}h(u,x,v)\,K_x(dv),
 \quad u\in\mathcal A.
\]
Joint measurability of \(h\) makes \(g_x\) measurable, and \(|h|\le B_Y\) makes every integral finite.  The simultaneous probability-one equality in \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\), evaluated at the random coordinate \(A\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) give
\[
 Y=Y(A)=h(A,X,V)\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every bounded Borel function \(\psi:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\), conditional independence \(V\perp A\mid X\) from \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}response\text{-}surface}\) and the definition of the conditional density \(f_x\) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\!\left[Y\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]
 &=E_P\!\left[h(A,x,V)\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]\\
 &=\int_{\mathcal A}\int_{\mathcal V}
       h(u,x,v)\psi(u)\,K_x(dv)f_x(u)\,du\\
 &=\int_{\mathcal A}g_x(u)\psi(u)f_x(u)\,du.
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, the definition \(m_x(u)=E_P[Y\mid A=u,X=x]\) implies
\[
 E_P\!\left[Y\psi(A)\mid X=x\right]
 =\int_{\mathcal A}m_x(u)\psi(u)f_x(u)\,du.
\]
Uniqueness of Radon--Nikodym derivatives therefore gives
\[
 m_x(u)=g_x(u)
 \quad\text{for }f_x(u)\,du\text{-almost every }u\in\mathcal A.
\]

We next remove this almost-everywhere qualification on \(I\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\), and \(\beta>3/2\), each of \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) has a continuous representative.  Indeed, for either function \(w\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat w(t)|\,dt
 \le
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{\beta}|\widehat w(t)|^2\,dt\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt\right\}^{1/2}<\infty.
\]
Thus its inverse Fourier integral is continuous by dominated convergence and equals \(w\) almost everywhere by Fourier inversion.  We use these continuous representatives.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}denominator}\) gives \(f_x(u)\ge\kappa>0\) on \(I\), so
\[
 \widetilde m_x(u):=\frac{q_x(u)}{f_x(u)},\qquad u\in I,
\]
is continuous.  Since \(q_x=m_xf_x\) by the definition of \(q_x\), the preceding almost-everywhere equality implies
\[
 \widetilde m_x(u)=g_x(u)
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }u\in I;
\]
the passage from \(f_x(u)\,du\)-null sets to Lebesgue-null sets uses \(f_x\ge\kappa\).  The map \(g_x\) is continuous on \(I\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}mean\text{-}continuity}\), because the structural representation gives
\[
 g_x(u)=E_P[Y(u)\mid X=x].
\]
Two continuous functions on the interval \(I\) that agree Lebesgue-almost everywhere agree everywhere: otherwise continuity would produce a nonempty relative open subinterval on which their difference is bounded away from zero, contradicting almost-everywhere equality.  Hence, for every \(u\in I\),
\[
 E_P[Y(u)\mid X=x]=g_x(u)=\widetilde m_x(u)=\frac{q_x(u)}{f_x(u)}.
\]

Because \(\mathcal X\) is finite, the law of total expectation now gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mu(a)
 &=E_P[Y(a)] &&\text{by the definition of \(\mu\)}\\
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xE_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]
    &&\text{by conditioning on the finite partition generated by \(X\)}\\
 &=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
    &&\text{by the pointwise bridge proved above}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the relationship between the causal target and the regression functional; it has not been imposed as a definition.  Finally, \(p_x\) is the observed marginal probability of \(X=x\), while \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\) makes every \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Division is legitimate on \(I\) by \(f_x\ge\kappa\), so the displayed causal curve is point identified from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

The structural condition is compatible with the fixed-nuisance common-uniform Bernoulli lower construction.  Given its continuous conditional means \(b_{j,n,x}:\mathcal A\to[1/4,3/4]\), take a single \(V\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) independent of \((A,X,U_1,U_2)\), and put
\[
 h_{j,n}(u,x,v)=\mathbf 1\{v\le b_{j,n,x}(u)\},
 \qquad
 Y_{j,n}(u)=h_{j,n}(u,X,V).
\]
Then \(h_{j,n}\) is jointly measurable, \(V\perp A\mid X\), consistency holds after setting \(Y_{j,n}=Y_{j,n}(A)\), and
\[
 E[Y_{j,n}(u)\mid X=x]=b_{j,n,x}(u),
\]
which is continuous.  Since \(B_Y\ge1\), these schedules also obey the frozen outcome bound, and no measurement-error condition is changed.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
There exist a standard Borel measurable space \((\mathcal V,\mathscr V)\), a \(\mathcal V\)-valued random element \(V\), and a jointly measurable map \(h:\mathcal A\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal V\to[-B_Y,B_Y]\) such that \(V\perp A\mid X\) and
\[
 P\bigl(Y(a)=h(a,X,V)\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\bigr)=1.
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: The frozen coordinatewise weak-unconfoundedness condition does not control evaluation at the random dose. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element rules out the diagonal-null-set witness and supplies the conditional-product calculation used in the causal bridge. It remains compatible with the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower construction by taking one independent common uniform random variable and thresholding it at the continuous conditional mean.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a standard structural exogeneity condition. It does not assume the ADRF formula, analytic identification, a stability modulus, a rate, or the lower-bound separation, and it leaves every measurement-error condition unchanged.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(a\in I\), the ADRF is point identified by \(\mu(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\), where every term on the right is a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).
proposed.justification: This connects the analytically identified marked transform to the causal dose-response curve through an explicit structural exogeneity bridge and pointwise-version regularity.
proposed.gap: Huang and Zhang identify this target under a known everywhere-nonzero error transform; the present result uses blind asymmetric replicates with spectral gaps, while making the causal response-surface condition explicit.
proposed.consumer: The formula is the population target for a simultaneous uncertainty display over the scientifically relevant dose interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem's claim is unchanged, but its proof uses the structural response-surface condition, causal-mean continuity, cell positivity, Sobolev continuity, and the density lower bound directly. The rejected cylinder-sigma-field condition is not used, and the redundant weak-unconfoundedness edge is removed from this theorem.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The constrained-sieve embedding and the quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus at order \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) remain unproved.
open_obligations.obstruction: Local qualitative identifiability supplies no uniform singular-value estimate. The frozen construction supplies neither a proved stability inequality for the bilinear grid map with two unknown atomic error factors nor a shape-preserving Jackson operator that simultaneously preserves normalization, the lower bound on \(I\), both Sobolev-radius constraints, and \(|q|\le B_Yf\).
open_obligations.attempted: The simultaneous empirical-transform event and global clipping bound were proved. Direct interpolation was then tested, but it neither controls the unknown error factors in the discrete bilinear cocycle nor preserves the nonlinear density and marked-sieve constraints.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The simultaneous confidence event and clipping assertions are proved.  Conditional on the cell labels, each probability-channel summand has modulus at most one and each marked-channel summand has modulus at most \(B_Y\).  Applying the real bounded-variable exponential inequality to real and imaginary parts gives, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|
 >2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)
 \le4e^{-\lambda_n},
\]
and the analogous inequality for \(\widehat G_{x,n}\) with radius \(2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\).  When \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the deterministic bounds \(|\widehat F_{x,n}-F_x|\le2\) and \(|\widehat G_{x,n}-G_x|\le2B_Y\) apply.  A union bound over the two channels, all \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\) costs at most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), this proves the claimed weaker bound \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\).  Also, every feasible \(\mu_\theta\) lies in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), and the endpoint rule therefore gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), including the empty-set convention.  What remains unproved is the constrained-sieve embedding and the deterministic inverse estimate
\[
 \sup_{\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}
 \|\mu_\theta-\mu_{\theta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \lesssim K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}.
\]

open_obligations.what_is_open: The upper theorem now has its pointwise causal bridge, but it still requires the feasible constrained-sieve embedding and the deterministic analytic stability bound from \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Without those deterministic assertions, the true approximating tuple is not known to belong to \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and empirical residual control cannot bound the diameter of the profiled ADRF set. Thus neither uniform coverage of the stated construction nor its \(r_n\) width follows yet.
open_obligations.attempted: The coverage and expected-width reduction was completed conditional on feasible embedding and the inverse modulus, including the regular-count split, the \(o(r_n)\) multinomial term, and the exponentially small count-failure remainder.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The causal bridge needed for coverage is supplied by the proved \(\mathrm{thm{:}adrf\text{-}id}\).  Conditional on the two unresolved deterministic assertions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\), the rest of the upper theorem follows.  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), a feasible approximating tuple \(\bar\theta\) satisfying \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\) and the profiled endpoint definitions imply \(L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\).  On the regular-count event, the deterministic feasible-set diameter and the two endpoint inflations give
\[
 W_n\le C\left\{K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}\right\}\le C'r_n,
\]
because \(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{1/2-\beta})\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}=o(r_n)\).  On count failure, \(W_n\le2B_Y\), while \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) bounds its probability by \(|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\).  Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le C'r_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}
 =O(r_n).
\]
Thus the remaining obstruction is deterministic analytic stability and feasible sieve embedding, not causal identification or an additional probabilistic argument.

prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification recovers the latent density and marked channel despite remote spectral zeros, and an explicit structural response-surface condition together with causal-mean continuity proves the pointwise causal bridge. The proposed empirical-characteristic-function inversion uses compact signal and error sieves and targets width \(r_n=(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\), but its constrained-sieve embedding and uniform analytic stability modulus remain unproved. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus also remains open, so no matched honest-band rate is yet claimed.

project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning supports local cocycle inversion, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve.
project_justification.fill: The candidate statistical construction specifies deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic-sieve dimensions; finite-sample simultaneous radii for the probability, marked, and multinomial coordinates; a compact joint feasibility set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. The causal bridge is proved under the explicit structural and continuity conditions. The remaining upper-side task is a shape-preserving feasible embedding and a quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus; the lower-side task is the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus. Until both are proved, the advertised \(r_n\) rate is a target rather than an established matched rate.

sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have finite-stratum \(X_i\), compact latent dose \(A_i\), and bounded potential-outcome schedules generated simultaneously as \(Y_i(a)=h(a,X_i,V_i)\) by a jointly measurable response surface, with \(V_i\perp A_i\mid X_i\); the stratum-specific causal means are continuous on \(I\).

prose_updates.interpretation: The observed two-channel law identifies the continuous regression curve \(q_x/f_x\). Structural exogeneity first equates this curve with the stratum-specific causal mean almost everywhere in dose; positivity and continuity then extend the equality to every target dose. Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness and almost-sure consistency alone would not suffice because they permit treatment-dependent diagonal modifications on null sets.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The pointwise causal bridge is closed by the structural response-surface and continuity conditions, and the qualitative marked identification is already established. The upper claim still stands or falls on a uniform discrete analytic-cocycle stability inequality and a shape-preserving constrained-sieve embedding. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus remains the separate lower-bound kernel.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The fixed values of \(\beta\), the Sobolev radii, \(p_{\min}\), the moment and local spectral constants, and \(\kappa\) are known class indices. Causal interpretation additionally uses a jointly measurable structural response surface with an exogenous latent variable and continuity of each stratum-specific causal mean on \(I\); these conditions are compatible with the common-uniform Bernoulli lower construction and do not strengthen measurement-error assumptions. Adaptation, growing replicate counts, boundary bands, and computational optimization remain outside scope. The explicit simultaneous upper band and matching all-band converse are not yet established because the analytic stability and fixed-nuisance lower-modulus steps remain open.

statement_notes.justification: This result now proves, rather than assumes, the bridge from the analytically identified marked regression to the point-dose causal response under a genuine jointly measurable structural response surface and causal-mean continuity.
statement_notes.gap: The measurement-error novelty remains blind asymmetric replication with possible spectral gaps; the causal interpretation is explicitly conditional on structural exogeneity and pointwise-version regularity.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the causal population curve that the simultaneous band is intended to cover and is compatible with common-uniform Bernoulli lower alternatives.

statement_notes.justification: The concentration-event and clipping components are proved, while constrained feasible embedding and the quantitative bilinear inverse modulus remain the exact upper-side kernel.
statement_notes.gap: Qualitative analytic continuation does not provide the required uniform singular-value control or preserve the nonlinear spline constraints.
statement_notes.consumer: Once completed, this lemma converts the explicit finite-dimensional confidence set into simultaneous coverage and deterministic width control.

statement_notes.justification: The causal and probabilistic reductions are complete conditional on analytic-sieve feasibility and stability; those deterministic premises remain unproved.
statement_notes.gap: No claimed comparator supplies the missing uniform marked-quotient stability result for two blind asymmetric error factors.
statement_notes.consumer: Completion would provide whole-curve uncertainty for the Melaku--Shi (2026) two-recall diet--mortality analysis.
